datasets_evaluated.evidence: The model was trained on benign BoT-IoT traffic and evaluated in both in-dataset and cross-dataset scenarios.

label_source.evidence: Three publicly available IoT intrusion datasets are used: the BoT-IoT, IoT-23, and ToN-IoT.

label_feature_overlap.evidence: The framework models benign encrypted IoT traffic using probabilistic latent representations and identifies anomalies through reconstruction-error-based scoring.

features_used.evidence: In TLS-aware IoT anomaly detection, this is especially valuable because the model must infer normal and abnormal behaviour from observable metadata such as TLS versions, cypher suites, JA3/JA3S fingerprints, packet-length distributions, and inter-arrival timing patterns, rather than from decrypted packet payloads.

feature_groups.evidence: Zeek and CICFlowMeter to construct a unified metadata feature space incorporating flow statistics and TLS attributes such as JA3 and JA3S fingerprints.

cert_fields_read.evidence: As payload inspection becomes impractical in encrypted environments, anomaly detection must instead rely on flow-level statistics and TLS metadata.

fingerprints_used.evidence: Zeek (Version 6.0; The Zeek Project, https://zeek.org) [24] is used to extract connection-level logs and TLS metadata, including protocol versions, cypher suites, extensions, server name indication (SNI), and cryptographic fingerprints such as JA3 and JA3S [12].

model_family.evidence: We introduce a TLS-aware anomaly detection framework that combines a β-Variational Autoencoder (β-VAE) with a hybrid ANOVA–Mutual Information (ANOVA–MI) feature-selection pipeline.

split_protocols.evidence: The model was trained on benign BoT-IoT traffic and evaluated in both in-dataset and cross-dataset scenarios.

main_split.evidence: The proposed approach is evaluated under both in-dataset and strict cross-dataset conditions using three heterogeneous benchmark datasets (BoT-IoT, IoT-23, and ToN-IoT).

easy_vs_hard_reported.evidence: The model achieves strong in-dataset performance on BoT-IoT (ROC-AUC ≈0.9996; F1 ≈0.9922) and retains robust anomaly-ranking and threshold-based detection capability under cross-dataset domain shift

shortcut_check.evidence: Relative to the no-selection configuration, all three feature-selection variants substantially improve F1-score across BoT-IoT, IoT-23, and ToN-IoT while reducing the input dimensionality from 30 to 20 features.

metrics.evidence: The model achieves strong in-dataset performance on BoT-IoT (ROC-AUC ≈0.9996; F1 ≈0.9922) and retains robust anomaly-ranking and threshold-based detection capability under cross-dataset domain shift

granularity.evidence: The per-flow detection model classifies each network flow independently.

first_n_packets.evidence: Raw PCAP traffic is processed using Zeek and CICFlowMeter to construct a unified metadata feature space incorporating flow statistics and TLS attributes such as JA3 and JA3S fingerprints.

cost_reported.evidence: The latency distribution (Figure 18) shows that the mean per-flow inference time is approximately 161 μs, with a 95th-percentile latency of 236 μs.

hardware.evidence: Training time (BoT-IoT) ≈33 s on a standard CPU (Intel Core i7, no GPU required)
